gap: No result ChatGPT got states OutdoorGearLab's scale weights from one reviewer and one method (Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23): Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 24.4 lb, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 25.0 lb, Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 25.2 lb, EcoFlow DELTA 3 28.1 lb. On that scale the Jackery stays lightest by 0.6 lb rather than the maker gap of 1.1 to 1.2 lb, and the Anker falls behind the BLUETTI, the reverse of the maker order every rival repeats.
standout_why: Solar Power Auditor's camping guide and Jackery review (cited in two chats) already give its own scale weights and bench usable Wh: Jackery 23.8 lb / 905 Wh, Anker 24.9 lb / 884 Wh, BLUETTI 25.0 lb / 892 Wh, DELTA 3 27.6 lb / 862 Wh. Its weights equal the maker figures exactly. Backup-power.org, Amphourly, KeepLights, JuiceBench, OutageReadyHQ and Volt & Valley give only maker specs, and each says so. So rivals already have measured weight and usable Wh. What they lack is a second, independent scale (OutdoorGearLab). It shows every unit at or above its spec weight, puts the Anker behind the BLUETTI, and gives usable Wh per measured pound. Our current page cites OGL's 24.4 lb for the Jackery but also says 'no reviewer has published a scale reading', which contradicts it and should be fixed.
decides: Confirms the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 as the lightest. Two independent scales (OGL 24.4 lb, Solar Power Auditor 23.8 lb) and two capacity tests (910 Wh and 905 Wh) put it first on both weight and usable Wh per pound: 910/24.4 = 37.3 Wh/lb, against 35.6 for the BLUETTI and 35.3 for the Anker. It also changes the runner-up. On OGL's scale the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (25.0 lb) is lighter than the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (25.2 lb), so 'only 1.1 lb heavier' for the Anker becomes 0.8 lb, and the BLUETTI is the second-lightest. The page should present weight as a range across scales, not one maker figure.

findings.label: Measured usable energy (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.source_title: OutdoorGearLab: Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 review (Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23)
findings.note: Measured with OGL's light-bar load bank. The text says 87% but the spec table says 'Usable Capacity 80%'. 890/1,024 = 86.9%, so the 87% in the text is the consistent figure. Usable Wh per measured lb: 890/25.2 = 35.3. Measured average charging rate 1,097 Wh/hr.

findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (Gidon, The Technology Man, 2025-11-04)
findings.note: Ran just over 54 min at 1 kW, metered with an energy-monitoring plug. Lost 20% in 12 h with no load and power-saving off, about 17 W. Full charge in 47 min at the 1,600 W setting. 42 dB at 1 m while charging at full speed. Weight given as 11.3 kg.

findings.note: European version; Notebookcheck warns the US unit differs in some points. Discharged until shutoff at 1%. Measured 1,110 Wh going in on AC charge, about 92% charge efficiency. Charge time just under 55 min without Boost. About 45 dB at 1 m under higher load.
